feed.title: Productivity & Everyday Tools — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Asana
entry.summary: A project-management platform tracking team work, tasks and workflows. Compared with Jira it suits non-software teams better and is lighter to set up, with fewer development-specific features.

entry.title: Awesome Calculators
entry.summary: A list of calculator tools for every platform. Unlike a single calculator, it arranges options by platform — desktop, mobile, web, command line.

entry.title: Awesome No-Login Web Apps
entry.summary: A list of useful web apps that work without login. Unlike general tool lists, it picks only those with no sign-up — use them at once without handing over data.

entry.title: Awesome Userscripts
entry.summary: A list of userscripts that enhance your browsing experience. Unlike browser extensions, they are small scripts with readable source that run under a manager such as Tampermonkey.

entry.title: Full Page Screen Capture
entry.summary: A Chrome extension that captures an entire page — scrolling included — as one image. Compared with DevTools’ hidden full-size screenshot command it is one click, and can save as PDF too.

entry.title: Google Keep
entry.summary: A quick sticky-note tool synced in the cloud, with lists, reminders and voice notes. Unlike Notion or Obsidian it wins on speed — you jot without building structure; the trade-off is limited formatting and linking.

entry.title: Jira
entry.summary: Agile project management with strong issue and release tracking for software teams. Compared with Trello it is heavy with a longer learning curve, but built for large teams that need sprints, workflows and reporting.

entry.title: Notion
entry.summary: A tool combining notes, wikis, databases and project boards in one workspace. Unlike Obsidian it is cloud-based and team-oriented; in exchange your data is not local files and offline use is limited.

entry.title: ProtectedText
entry.summary: An encrypted online notepad that needs no registration; the password never leaves your browser. Unlike Pastebin, the server never sees the note in plain text.

entry.title: Slack
entry.summary: A team-communication platform organised by channels, with tool integrations. Compared with Discord it is work-oriented with a strong integration ecosystem; the free plan limits message history to 90 days.

entry.title: Todoist
entry.summary: A to-do tool for personal and team projects, focused on fast capture. Unlike all-purpose tools such as Notion it focuses solely on tasks, and understands natural-language dates like “tomorrow at 9”.

entry.title: Trello
entry.summary: A simple task tool managing projects with cards and boards (Kanban), owned by Atlassian. Compared with Jira it takes minutes to set up, but does not meet large teams’ reporting needs.

entry.title: Image Max URL
entry.summary: A browser extension that finds the largest/original version of an image or video from its shrunken form. Unlike right-click “open image” it reverses the resizing: it resolves the full-resolution source from a thumbnail URL.

entry.title: Everything
entry.summary: Instant filename search on Windows, built by reading the NTFS master file table directly. That is the trick against Windows Search: it does not index content, so the first scan takes seconds and results appear as you type.

entry.title: Microsoft PowerToys
entry.summary: The official set of tools that adds what Windows lacks: window layouts (FancyZones), bulk rename, colour picker, text extraction. Unlike third-party equivalents it is built and kept open source by Microsoft, so updates do not break it.

entry.title: Rufus
entry.summary: A Windows tool for writing bootable USB drives that works out the UEFI/BIOS and partitioning details itself. What sets it apart from other writers is the option to strip the TPM and account requirements out of a Windows 11 install.

entry.title: Snapdrop
entry.summary: Browser-to-browser file transfer between devices on the same network, connected directly over WebRTC. Unlike AirDrop it does not care about the operating system — Android to Mac works — and needs no install or account.

entry.title: GitHub Gist
entry.summary: Shares single-file snippets with version history; comments and forking make it more durable than a pastebin.

entry.title: Pastebin
entry.summary: The simplest way to share text or a log, with syntax highlighting and expiry. Unlike GitHub Gist it needs no account; remember not to paste anything sensitive.

entry.title: Udeler GUI
entry.summary: Downloads Udemy courses you own for offline viewing; the repository was archived in 2024. Unlike the Udemy app’s offline mode the files stay with you — though it may no longer work on Udemy’s DRM-protected courses.

entry.title: AppList
entry.summary: A text-list app launcher for iPhone. Unlike the default icon grid it removes attention-grabbing colourful icons — deliberate friction on the digital minimalism side.

entry.title: MacroDroid
entry.summary: Builds trigger-action rules on Android — Wi-Fi on when you reach a location, silent while charging. Less powerful than Tasker and vastly more comprehensible.

entry.title: Siteyi Çevrimdışı İndirme
entry.summary: A guide comparing methods for archiving a site offline — wget, HTTrack and the rest. Unlike a single tool’s docs it sets the methods side by side; practical preparation for documentation at risk of vanishing.
